entry_points.summary: Amend SPEC/PLAN/TASKS or FIX.md; uses $Z_HARNESS_PLAN_DIR; re-classifies complexity stamps for changed task blocks.
Read-only pre-implementation plan audit; verifies SPEC/PLAN/TASKS, writes PLAN_AUDIT_REPORT.md, routes via route-decision.md.
Three-vendor parallel ideation (Claude + consultant-primary + consultant-secondary) with mandatory anti-bias check; produces BRAINSTORM.md.
Heavy hypothesis-tournament pipeline: Phase 0 wrong-tool gate, rounds of parallel hypothesis generation, fix with /z-plan-light mechanics, mandatory post-mortem.
Lightest harness on-ramp: no plan artifacts, doc-fetcher grounding, inline implementation, mandatory reviewer gate; logs to z-harness/adhoc/.

Full task-queue orchestrator: --tasks fast path, tree-rooted MANIFEST support, spec-precheck, TESTS.md integration, compaction breakpoints (Z_IMPLEMENT_PAUSE_TASKS/MINUTES), cross_task_notes propagation, hard caps MAX_ATTEMPTS/wall-clock/halts.
Single-task implementation; model selected from **Complexity:** stamp; no auto-retry; single-shot design forces fresh context per task.
Post-run retro: reads events.jsonl friction signals, proposes <=5 z-harness edits, applies accepted edits, invokes /z-suggest-memory with derived concept_hints.
Bootstraps two-tier docs: doc-updater per concept, INDEX.json aggregation, TAGS.txt 15-tag seed, MEMORIES-FLAT.md init via regenerate-memories-flat.py.

Refreshes stale concept docs: doc-updater with dedup_tags:true, Phase 2.3 pre-audit compaction breakpoint (--audit only) with .maintain_docs_audit_state.json fast-forward, stale-memory UI, TAG_COLLISIONS surface, MEMORIES-FLAT.md regen.
Lightweight planner for small fixes: inline orchestrator implementation, FIX.md only, mandatory reviewer gate, auto-bail at >5 files or >2 non-obvious decisions.
Scope splitter into 2-6 clusters: kebab-slug security gate, file-overlap reconciliation from TASKS.md canonical, MANIFEST.md + SHARED-CONCERNS.md output.
Full rigorous planning: docs-freshness gate, Explore cap 3, batch decisions, single bundled cross-LLM consult, parallel Haiku complexity classifier per task.
Terrain mapping: cost gate, doc-fetcher first, up to 3 parallel Explore subagents, bundled cross-LLM critique, mandatory ## No-recommendation section.

Final-gate two-pronged review: Phase 3.5 runs TESTS.md suite (blocker on failure), Phase 3.7 mandatory pre-consult compaction breakpoint with .review_state.json fast-forward, parallel consultants on cumulative diff, promotes findings to REVIEW-TASKS.md.
Read-only diagnostic: shell+jq+awk only, no subagent calls; wall time, token spend, halts, stalls, plugin version history, suggested next command.
Sole authoring path for memories[]: append/edit/delete modes, schema validation, atomic writes, MEMORIES-FLAT.md regen, optional human-tier refresh. Default: Cancel.
Semantic test-case planner: risk-ranks tasks, requires non-trivial failure classes, cross-LLM consult drops trivial drafts, writes TESTS.md + cross-links into TASKS.md.

invariants: All plan artifact paths are resolved through scripts/plan-path.sh to $Z_HARNESS_PLAN_DIR; no skill hardcodes z-harness/<slug>/ paths.
Cross-LLM consult agents are always referenced as consultant-primary and consultant-secondary; code review uses the reviewer agent.
Phase telemetry (log-phase.sh start/end) is mandatory for every skill execution.
Review-generated spec-gap tasks are inputs to z-amend and must not authorize implementers to mutate planning artifacts directly.
All skills implement idempotent run patterns; re-running modifies only targeted resources.
z-suggest-memory is the sole path for creating, editing, or deleting memories[] entries; doc-updater only copies them verbatim.

Planning-family skills share the route policy: route bails write route-decision.md, emit plan_route_decision, preserve existing telemetry, present an AskUser handoff, and stop instead of auto-running the target command.

z-implement-all compaction breakpoints fire only at batch-settle boundaries (after atomic TASKS.md write, after batch_done event, after all halt signals resolved); the compaction_pause event and push-notify exit the loop cleanly without running Finalize.
z-review-all Phase 3.7 always runs between Phase 3.5 and Phase 4; it is skipped only when Pre-Phase-0 resume check fast-forwards past it (state file present, HEAD matches, artifact files exist).
z-maintain-docs --audit Phase 2.3 state file fast-forward is valid only when stale_concepts_at_ack equals the current stale concept set; differing sets invalidate and delete the state file.
gotchas: z-implement-all --tasks <path> skips slug discovery, tree validation, and ack/force-partial gates; $BASE is derived from the task file's parent directory.
z-implement-all compaction breakpoint counters (tasks_since_pause, pause_clock_start) are in-memory only and reset on every re-invocation — TASKS.md [x] count is the durable state, not the counters.

z-implement-all cross_task_notes: missing target task IDs emit cross_task_note_target_missing warning event but do not fail the producing task; the note write is part of the same atomic TASKS.md update as the [~]→[x] flip.
z-plan-split uses two distinct per-cluster identifiers: cluster_id (C1..CN) for telemetry, cluster_slug (kebab-case) for on-disk paths - never swap them.
z-implement-all hard caps (MAX_ATTEMPTS=2, MAX_TASK_WALL_MS=45min, MAX_DISTINCT_HALTS=3) are unconditional and cannot be caught by skip-marker text matching.
z-debug Phase 0 wrong-tool gate is non-skippable: if user already has a hypothesis, skill exits with /z-fix recommendation.
z-review-all Phase 3.5 TESTS.md suite run is a blocker gate - any test failure halts the review before consultants are spawned.
z-review-all .review_state.json is deleted unconditionally at Phase 6 cleanup (whether REVIEW-TASKS.md was generated or shipped.md was written) so a subsequent /z-review-all starts a full fresh run.
z-maintain-docs --audit Phase 2.3 state file (docs/llm/.maintain_docs_audit_state.json) is deleted in Phase 5 cleanup regardless of how the audit ended.
z-suggest-memory and z-init-docs both write docs/llm/TAGS.txt with the same 15-tag controlled seed via atomic write; neither overwrites if the file already exists.

Route classes are distinct: primary targets are /z-do, /z-plan-light, /z-plan, /z-plan-split, /z-brainstorm, and /z-research; contextual exits are /z-audit-plan, /z-fix, /z-debug, /z-amend, and /z-maintain-docs.

Contextual exits require their preconditions: /z-audit-plan needs existing SPEC/PLAN/TASKS, /z-amend needs an existing plan to modify, /z-fix needs a diagnosis, /z-debug needs an unknown-cause symptom, and /z-maintain-docs needs relevant docs drift.
